The docs for the IsApply family of typeclasses state:

For every type that declares a FunLike instance and an Add instance, there should be generally an IsAddApply instance with the proof usually being rfl].

(and presumably same goes for Sub, etc). Personally I had no idea these typeclasses existed, and just discovered it today while try to understand why for me a simp call didn't work as well as it did in a similar theorem in mathlib.

Is it feasible/advisable to have a linter for this?

If we enable such linter... In my draft #39826, I have a new FunLike + Add type that doesn't satisfy the strong IsAddApply (it satisfies the weak =[codiscreteWithin U]). Does it mean I did some wrong, like I should use CoeFun instead of FunLike?

In this case you don't have a add_apply lemma, so all is good. Same thing with bundled Lp functions. Other excepts are matrices (because two arguments) and something like docs#MeasureTheory.Measure.sub_apply
